questions.q: What makes two consumers members of the same consumer group?
options: They were started within the same second
They run on the same physical machine
They set the same `group.id`
They subscribe to the same topic, regardless of group.id
questions.explain: group.id is what defines group membership — it's the setting the group coordinator uses to assign partitions.

questions.q: What guarantee does Kafka make about partition assignment within one consumer group?
options: Partitions are assigned randomly and can change on every poll() call
Every member of the group reads every partition simultaneously
Each partition is assigned to exactly one member of that group at a time
Only the first consumer to join ever gets any partitions
questions.explain: This is what turns a consumer group into one logical, horizontally scaled consumer — no partition is double-assigned within a group.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT typically trigger a rebalance?
options: A new consumer joining the group
The topic's partition count changing
An existing consumer crashing (detected via a missed heartbeat)
A consumer in a completely different consumer group committing its offset
questions.explain: Rebalances are triggered by changes within the group's own membership or the topic's partition count — a different group's activity is irrelevant.

questions.q: If a topic has 3 partitions and a consumer group has 5 members, what happens to the 2 extra consumers?
options: They each get a duplicate copy of an existing partition's data
They sit idle, with no partition assigned, since Kafka never assigns more than one consumer per partition within a group
The group refuses to start until the extra consumers are removed
They automatically create 2 new partitions to use
questions.explain: Parallelism in a group is capped by partition count — a partition is the smallest unit of work a group can divide.

questions.q: What's the only way to actually put idle extra consumers to work in that same scenario?
options: Lower their group.id value
Increase the topic's partition count so there are more units of parallelism to assign
Restart the idle consumers repeatedly until Kafka assigns them a partition anyway
Nothing can be done — idle consumers can never be used
questions.explain: Since a partition can only go to one consumer at a time within a group, more usable parallelism requires more partitions, not more consumers.
